items.title: FDA overview: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
items.authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
items.summary: FDA describes idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis as a rare, serious lung disease that causes scarring around the air sacs in the lungs. The scarring can make breathing harder and the condition can worsen at different speeds.

conditionOverview.whatItIs: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is a serious lung disease that causes scarring in the lungs. The scarring can make breathing harder over time.
conditionOverview.whatToWatch: Shortness of breath, a dry cough, tiredness, and changes in activity can matter. IPF can worsen slowly or more quickly.
conditionOverview.researchPath: Breathing tests, scan results, oxygen needs, current medicine, and disease stage can change which treatments, support, and trials are worth discussing.

items.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (an Update) and Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Adults: An Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline
items.authors: Raghu G, Remy-Jardin M, Richeldi L, et al.
items.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
items.summary: The current authoritative IPF practice guideline jointly endorsed by the American Thoracic Society, European Respiratory Society, Japanese Respiratory Society, and Latin American Thoracic Association. Updates the 2018 guideline. Contains strong recommendations for pirfenidone and nintedanib, introduces the concept of 'progressive pulmonary fibrosis' as a treatable phenotype beyond IPF, and recommends against prednisone monotherapy or combination immunosuppression for IPF.

keyPassages.quote: We recommend treatment with nintedanib or pirfenidone for patients with IPF (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence).
We recommend against treatment of IPF with the combination of prednisone, azathioprine, and N-acetylcysteine (strong recommendation, low-quality evidence).
In patients with PPF (other than IPF) who have failed standard management for the suspected underlying ILD, nintedanib is recommended (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence).

items.title: Diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: An Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline
items.authors: Raghu G, Remy-Jardin M, Myers JL, et al.
items.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
items.summary: The diagnostic counterpart to the treatment guideline. Defines the HRCT and histopathology patterns required for IPF diagnosis: Definite UIP, Probable UIP, Indeterminate, and Alternative Diagnosis. Establishes that Definite UIP pattern on HRCT in the right clinical context is sufficient for IPF diagnosis without surgical lung biopsy.

keyPassages.quote: A UIP pattern on HRCT is characterized by subpleural, basal predominant fibrosis with honeycombing, with or without traction bronchiectasis.

items.title: Pirfenidone in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (CAPACITY): two randomised trials
items.authors: Noble PW, Albera C, Bradford WZ, et al.
items.summary: The pair of phase 3 RCTs (CAPACITY 004 and 006) that led to pirfenidone's approval for IPF. Enrolled 779 patients with mild-to-moderate IPF. CAPACITY 004 met its primary endpoint (FVC decline); CAPACITY 006 did not, leading the FDA to initially withhold approval and request ASCEND.

keyPassages.quote: In study 004, pirfenidone reduced decline in FVC (p=0.001). Mean FVC change at week 72 was -8.0% in the pirfenidone 2403 mg/day group versus -12.4% in the placebo group.

items.title: A phase 3 trial of pirfenidone in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
items.authors: King TE Jr, Bradford WZ, Castro-Bernardini S, et al.
items.summary: The confirmatory phase 3 RCT that secured US FDA approval of pirfenidone (Esbriet) in October 2014. 555 patients; at 52 weeks, pirfenidone reduced the proportion of patients with FVC decline >=10% or death from 31% to 17%. Mortality was reduced in a pooled analysis of ASCEND + CAPACITY.

keyPassages.quote: In the pirfenidone group, as compared with the placebo group, there was a relative reduction of 47.9% in the proportion of patients who had an absolute decline of 10 percentage points or more in the percentage of predicted FVC or who died.

In a pre-specified pooled analysis incorporating results from two previous phase 3 trials, the between-group difference favoring pirfenidone was significant for death from any cause (P=0.01) and from IPF (P=0.006).

items.title: Efficacy and safety of nintedanib in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2)
items.authors: Richeldi L, du Bois RM, Raghu G, et al.
items.summary: Twin phase 3 RCTs that secured US FDA approval of nintedanib (Ofev) in October 2014 on the same day as pirfenidone. 1,066 patients total. Both trials met the primary endpoint of reducing annual FVC decline. Diarrhea was the main adverse event (>60%).

keyPassages.quote: The adjusted annual rate of change in FVC was -114.7 mL with nintedanib versus -239.9 mL with placebo (difference, 125.3 mL; 95% CI, 77.7 to 172.9; P<0.001) in INPULSIS-1, and -113.6 mL versus -207.3 mL (difference, 93.7 mL; 95% CI, 44.8 to 142.7; P<0.001) in INPULSIS-2.
Diarrhea was the most frequent adverse event, reported in 61.5% and 63.2% of patients receiving nintedanib in the two trials, versus 18.6% and 18.3% in the placebo groups.

items.title: Nintedanib in progressive fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (INBUILD)
items.authors: Flaherty KR, Wells AU, Cottin V, et al.
items.summary: Expanded nintedanib's indication beyond IPF to any chronic fibrosing ILD with a progressive phenotype (chronic HP, connective tissue disease-ILD, unclassifiable ILD, sarcoidosis, etc.). Foundation for the 2022 guideline's 'progressive pulmonary fibrosis' concept.

keyPassages.quote: The adjusted rate of decline in FVC was -80.8 mL per year in the nintedanib group and -187.8 mL per year in the placebo group (difference, 107.0 mL per year; 95% CI, 65.4 to 148.5; P<0.001).

items.title: Prednisone, azathioprine, and N-acetylcysteine for pulmonary fibrosis (PANTHER-IPF)
items.authors: Raghu G, Anstrom KJ, King TE Jr, et al. (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Clinical Research Network)
items.summary: CRITICAL NEGATIVE TRIAL. The triple-therapy arm (prednisone + azathioprine + NAC) was stopped early by the DSMB for increased mortality (8 vs 1 death), increased hospitalizations (23 vs 7), and more serious adverse events vs placebo. Ended decades of empiric use of combination immunosuppression for IPF. This is why current guidelines STRONGLY recommend against these regimens.

keyPassages.quote: The interim analysis showed that the prednisone-azathioprine-NAC group, as compared with the placebo group, had an increased rate of death (11% vs. 1%, P=0.01) and hospitalization (29% vs. 8%, P<0.001). These data, along with an increased number of serious adverse events, led to early termination of the combination-therapy group.

items.title: Randomized trial of acetylcysteine in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
items.authors: Martinez FJ, de Andrade JA, Anstrom KJ, King TE Jr, Raghu G (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Clinical Research Network)
items.summary: PANTHER-IPF's NAC-monotherapy arm. After the triple-therapy arm was stopped, the NAC-alone arm continued. It also showed NO benefit over placebo for FVC decline, mortality, or exacerbation. Put to rest the long-standing empiric use of NAC monotherapy for IPF despite common off-label enthusiasm.

keyPassages.quote: As compared with placebo, acetylcysteine offered no significant benefit with respect to the preservation of FVC in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and mild-to-moderate impairment in lung function.

items.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
items.authors: Lederer DJ, Martinez FJ
items.summary: The most widely-cited modern clinical review of IPF. Synthesizes epidemiology, pathogenesis, the HRCT-based diagnostic paradigm, both antifibrotics, supportive care, and transplant. The standard reference for the modern standard of care in IPF.

items.title: High prevalence of abnormal acid gastro-oesophageal reflux in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
items.authors: Raghu G, Freudenberger TD, Yang S, et al.
items.summary: Foundational observational pH-monitoring study reporting a high prevalence of abnormal acid gastro-oesophageal reflux in the studied IPF cohort. The study does not establish that antacid treatment improves IPF outcomes.

keyPassages.quote: Abnormal acid GOR was detected in 33 of 38 (87%) patients with IPF. Distal and proximal acid GOR was detected in 76% and 63%, respectively.

items.title: ESBRIET (pirfenidone) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.authors: Genentech / Roche
items.summary: Current FDA-approved label for pirfenidone (Esbriet). Indication: treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Target dose: 2403 mg/day (three 267 mg capsules three times daily with food) reached by three-week titration. Key warnings: hepatic function elevations (check LFTs monthly x6 then q3mo), photosensitivity/rash, GI (nausea, dyspepsia, diarrhea). Interaction: strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, enoxacin) are contraindicated; CYP1A2 inducers (smoking) reduce exposure.

keyPassages.quote: ESBRIET is indicated for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).
Elevations in ALT, AST, and bilirubin have been observed in patients treated with ESBRIET. Conduct LFTs prior to initiation, monthly for the first 6 months and then every 3 months thereafter.

Concomitant administration of ESBRIET with fluvoxamine or other strong CYP1A2 inhibitors is not recommended. Use of strong CYP1A2 inducers, including smoking, should be discontinued prior to and during ESBRIET treatment.

items.title: OFEV (nintedanib) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.authors: Boehringer Ingelheim
items.summary: Current FDA-approved label for nintedanib (Ofev). Indications: IPF, chronic fibrosing ILD with progressive phenotype (post-INBUILD), and systemic sclerosis-associated ILD. Dose: 150 mg BID with food. Key warnings: hepatotoxicity (LFTs baseline, monthly x3, q3mo; DILI reported), GI (diarrhea in ~62%, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain), arterial thromboembolic events, bleeding risk (antiplatelet/anticoagulant interaction), GI perforation, embryo-fetal toxicity. P-gp substrate — rifampin reduces exposure, ketoconazole increases it.

keyPassages.quote: OFEV is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF); for chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) with a progressive phenotype; and to slow the rate of decline in pulmonary function in patients with systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD).
Diarrhea was the most frequent gastrointestinal event, occurring in 62% of patients treated with OFEV compared to 18% of patients treated with placebo in INPULSIS trials.
Nintedanib is a VEGFR inhibitor and therefore may increase the risk of bleeding. In postmarketing use, non-serious and serious bleeding events, some of which were fatal, have been reported.

items.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
items.authors: Maher TM, Bendstrup E, Dron L, et al.
items.summary: Lancet seminar review on IPF epidemiology and management. Useful modern counterpart to the 2018 NEJM Lederer & Martinez review for clinician orientation.

items.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation for interstitial lung disease (Cochrane Review)
items.authors: Dowman L, Hill CJ, May A, Holland AE
items.summary: Cochrane systematic review establishing that pulmonary rehabilitation improves 6-minute walk distance, dyspnea, and HRQoL in ILD including IPF. Basis for guideline recommendations to enroll IPF patients in structured pulmonary rehab.

keyPassages.quote: Pulmonary rehabilitation improved exercise capacity compared with no pulmonary rehabilitation (mean difference 40.07 metres, 95% CI 32.70 to 47.44) in people with ILD.

items.title: ISHLT consensus document for lung transplant candidate selection — 2021 update
items.authors: Leard LE, Holm AM, Valapour M, et al.
items.journal: Journal of Heart and Lung Transplantation
items.summary: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation consensus on lung transplant candidate selection. IPF is the most common indication for lung transplantation worldwide. Patients with IPF and progressive disease despite antifibrotics should be referred early for transplant evaluation. Upper age limit is no longer absolute but physiological fitness matters.

keyPassages.quote: Early referral (at the time of diagnosis of ILD with a high risk of mortality or progression) is strongly recommended.

items.title: Treatment of Gastroesophageal Reflux in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.authors: Fidler L, Sitzer N, Shapera S, Shah PS
items.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of antireflux therapy (PPIs, H2 blockers, fundoplication) in IPF. Evidence is low-to-moderate quality: earlier post-hoc analyses suggested possible benefit, but pooled data did not show a significant effect on FVC decline, and some analyses raised infection concerns. Guidelines give only a conditional recommendation. Treat GERD when symptomatic; antireflux treatment should not be withheld in IPF, but it is not a proven disease-modifying therapy.

items.title: Stem cell-based therapy for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis — current status and future perspectives
items.authors: Glassberg MK, Csete I, Simonet E, Elliot SJ
items.summary: Reviews early-phase human stem cell trials for IPF. AETHER (phase 1, Glassberg 2017) and a small allogeneic MSC trial showed safety signals but NO proven efficacy. Cell source matters (bone-marrow MSC vs placental vs cord blood vs adipose). Commercial stem cell clinics (especially in China, Vietnam, Mexico, India) offer products with no peer-reviewed IPF efficacy data and multiple FDA warning letters to US-based operators who supply them.

items.title: Home oxygen therapy for adults with chronic lung disease — an official American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline
items.authors: Jacobs SS, Krishnan JA, Lederer DJ, et al.
items.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
items.summary: ATS guideline on home oxygen therapy. For adults with ILD (including IPF) and severe resting hypoxemia, long-term O2 is strongly recommended. For exertional desaturation (common in IPF), ambulatory O2 is conditionally recommended — it improves exercise capacity and symptoms in many patients.

keyPassages.quote: For adults with chronic lung disease who have severe exertional room-air hypoxemia, we recommend prescribing ambulatory oxygen (conditional recommendation, moderate-quality evidence).

items.title: Nintedanib with Add-on Pirfenidone in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Results of the INJOURNEY Trial
items.authors: Vancheri C, Kreuter M, Richeldi L, Ryerson CJ, et al.
items.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
items.summary: INJOURNEY: open-label trial of adding pirfenidone to background nintedanib in IPF. Primary objective was safety/tolerability, not efficacy. The combination was manageable in most patients over 12 weeks, with gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhea, nausea, vomiting) the main issue. Combination therapy is NOT standard of care — current guidelines do not recommend routine combination, but it is used case-by-case when one drug alone is insufficient and the patient tolerates both. Expect higher GI and hepatic monitoring burden.

keyPassages.quote: Nintedanib with add-on pirfenidone had a manageable safety and tolerability profile in patients with IPF, with gastrointestinal events the most frequent adverse events.

items.title: Trial of a Preferential Phosphodiesterase 4B Inhibitor for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (Phase 2)
items.authors: Richeldi L, Azuma A, Cottin V, Hesslinger C, Stowasser S, Valenzuela C, Wijsenbeek MS, Zoz DF, Voss F, Maher TM
items.summary: Phase 2 RCT of BI 1015550 (nerandomilast / Jascayd), a preferential PDE4B inhibitor, in IPF. At 12 weeks, treatment prevented FVC decline vs placebo — the readout that launched FIBRONEER-IPF / FIBRONEER-ILD. HISTORICAL context only: nerandomilast is now FDA-approved (Oct 7, 2025). Prefer the phase 3 FIBRONEER-IPF paper (ipf-fibroneer-ipf-2025) for efficacy numbers.

keyPassages.quote: Treatment with BI 1015550, either alone or with background antifibrotic therapy, prevented a decrease in lung function in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

items.title: Nerandomilast in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (FIBRONEER-IPF)
items.authors: Richeldi L, Azuma A, Cottin V, et al.
items.summary: PIVOTAL phase 3 RCT that secured FDA approval of nerandomilast (Jascayd) for IPF. 1,177 patients; 77.7% on background nintedanib or pirfenidone. Primary endpoint: absolute FVC change at week 52. Adjusted mean FVC changes: −114.7 mL (18 mg BID), −138.6 mL (9 mg BID), −183.5 mL (placebo). Adjusted difference vs placebo for the approved 18 mg dose: 68.8 mL (95% CI 30.3–107.4; P<0.001) — i.e. about 69 mL less FVC lost over 52 weeks, NOT 80 mL/year. Most common AE: diarrhea. This is the number to cite for nerandomilast efficacy.

keyPassages.quote: Adjusted mean changes in FVC at week 52 were −114.7 ml in the nerandomilast 18-mg group, −138.6 ml in the nerandomilast 9-mg group, and −183.5 ml in the placebo group. The adjusted difference between the nerandomilast 18-mg group and the placebo group was 68.8 ml (95% CI, 30.3 to 107.4; P<0.001).
A total of 1177 patients underwent randomization, of whom 77.7% were taking nintedanib or pirfenidone at enrollment.

items.title: JASCAYD (nerandomilast) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.authors: Boehringer Ingelheim
items.summary: FDA-approved label for nerandomilast (Jascayd), a preferential PDE4B inhibitor and the FIRST new-mechanism IPF drug in over a decade. FDA approved it for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis on October 7, 2025, and for progressive pulmonary fibrosis in December 2025, based on FIBRONEER-IPF (NEJM 2025; 1,177 patients; approved 18 mg BID slowed FVC loss by 68.8 mL vs placebo at week 52). Recommended dose: 18 mg orally twice daily (9 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors). Newest FDA-approved antifibrotic — list FIRST among approved IPF treatments. Never describe as investigational.

keyPassages.quote: JASCAYD is a phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor indicated for: the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in adult patients; the treatment of progressive pulmonary fibrosis in adult patients.
Recommended Dosage: 18 mg orally twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
In FIBRONEER-IPF, the adjusted difference in FVC change at week 52 between nerandomilast 18 mg twice daily and placebo was 68.8 mL (patients lost less lung function on nerandomilast).
Approval was based on FIBRONEER-IPF, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with IPF, with or without background antifibrotic therapy.

items.title: Metformin Does Not Affect Clinically Relevant Outcomes in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
items.authors: Spagnolo P, Kreuter M, Maher TM, et al.
items.summary: KEY HUMAN EVIDENCE ON METFORMIN IN IPF. A post-hoc analysis of 624 placebo-arm patients across three phase 3 pirfenidone trials (CAPACITY 004, CAPACITY 006, ASCEND) compared metformin users vs non-users. Metformin had NO effect on disease progression, FVC decline, 6-minute walk distance, hospitalization, or mortality. If anything, slightly more metformin users had a ≥5% FVC decline. Conclusion: metformin has no effect on clinically relevant outcomes in IPF. This means metformin HAS been studied in people with IPF — it is NOT an unstudied drug — and the human evidence does not support it as an IPF treatment.

keyPassages.quote: Metformin has no effect on clinically relevant outcomes in patients with IPF.
A higher proportion of metformin users compared with nonmetformin users had a relative FVC decline of >=5% (63.4 vs. 50.6%, p = 0.043).

items.title: Metformin reverses established lung fibrosis in a bleomycin model
items.authors: Rangarajan S, Bone NB, Zmijewska AA, et al.
items.summary: PRECLINICAL (ANIMAL/CELL) study that generated the metformin-for-IPF hypothesis. In mouse lungs and in fibroblasts from human IPF patients, activating AMPK with metformin reduced and even reversed established fibrosis. This is exciting laboratory science, but it is NOT human proof. It explains WHY metformin keeps coming up for IPF — but the human post-hoc data (Spagnolo 2018) did not show benefit. So research on metformin in IPF clearly exists; it is just not positive in people yet.

keyPassages.quote: In a bleomycin model of lung fibrosis in mice, metformin therapeutically accelerates the resolution of well-established fibrosis in an AMPK-dependent manner.

canonicalFacts.claim: Nerandomilast (brand name Jascayd) is FDA-approved for IPF (October 7, 2025) and for progressive pulmonary fibrosis (December 2025). The recommended dose is 18 mg by mouth twice daily, with or without background nintedanib or pirfenidone.
FIBRONEER-IPF (NEJM 2025): nerandomilast 18 mg twice daily slowed FVC decline vs placebo by an adjusted 68.8 mL at week 52 (mean change −114.7 mL vs −183.5 mL).
The FDA-approved disease-modifying treatments for IPF are pirfenidone (Esbriet), nintedanib (Ofev), and nerandomilast (Jascayd).
Metformin has been studied in people with IPF and did not improve outcomes in a post-hoc analysis of three phase 3 trials, despite promising laboratory and mouse studies.
In ASCEND, pirfenidone produced a 47.9% relative reduction in the proportion of patients with an absolute FVC decline of at least 10 percentage points or death versus placebo.

In INPULSIS-1, annual FVC decline was −114.7 mL with nintedanib versus −239.9 mL with placebo, a difference of 125.3 mL. In INPULSIS-2, annual FVC decline was −113.6 mL with nintedanib versus −207.3 mL with placebo, a difference of 93.7 mL.
In PANTHER-IPF, prednisone, azathioprine, and N-acetylcysteine combination therapy increased death and hospitalization compared with placebo.
Compared with placebo, acetylcysteine offered no significant benefit for preservation of FVC in patients with IPF and mild-to-moderate impairment.
~87% of IPF patients have abnormal acid gastroesophageal reflux on pH probe studies.
Pulmonary rehabilitation improved exercise capacity by a mean 40.07 metres versus no rehabilitation in people with interstitial lung disease.
IPF is the most common indication for lung transplantation worldwide; early referral is strongly recommended.
Pirfenidone is metabolized by CYP1A2. Smoking and strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, enoxacin) meaningfully affect exposure.
Nintedanib is a VEGFR inhibitor and increases bleeding risk — special caution with antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Treat gastroesophageal reflux when symptomatic; antireflux therapy is not proven to modify IPF progression.
Enroll in a structured pulmonary rehabilitation program — improves 6-minute walk distance, dyspnea, and quality of life.
For severe exertional room-air hypoxemia, discuss ambulatory oxygen as conditionally recommended by the ATS guideline.
Smoking induces CYP1A2 and reduces pirfenidone exposure.
Discuss early lung-transplant referral at diagnosis of interstitial lung disease with a high risk of mortality or progression.

literatureSearchSeeds.why: Frequently proposed as a repurposing candidate; human IPF data exists and must be fetched live on every query — not stored as static truth.
Common supplement hypothesis in IPF; observational literature should be retrieved live.

redFlags: Literature warns against prednisone + azathioprine + N-acetylcysteine triple therapy — PANTHER-IPF showed increased mortality and hospitalization. This is a STRONG GUIDELINE-LEVEL contraindication.
Literature warns against prednisone monotherapy for IPF (as opposed to acute exacerbation or a mimicker like NSIP). Chronic steroids have not been shown to benefit IPF and cause harm.
Literature warns against NAC monotherapy for IPF — PANTHER-NAC showed no benefit.

Literature warns against seeking stem cell treatment from clinics in China, Vietnam, Mexico, or India. There is no peer-reviewed efficacy data for IPF and multiple FDA warning letters to US-based operators who source from these labs.

Evidence suggests increased risk when combining nintedanib with full-dose anticoagulation without specialist input — VEGFR inhibition increases bleeding risk, and fatal bleeding events are reported in post-marketing surveillance.
FDA label contraindicates co-prescribing fluvoxamine, enoxacin, or other strong CYP1A2 inhibitors with pirfenidone.
Acute worsening of dyspnea <1 month with new bilateral ground-glass on HRCT = possible acute exacerbation of IPF. Hospital mortality ~50%. Urgent pulmonology/ICU referral.

pipelineDrugs.name: Nerandomilast
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Preferential PDE4B inhibitor — anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-APPROVED for IPF on October 7, 2025 (brand name Jascayd); also approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis December 2025. Oral, 18 mg twice daily. FIBRONEER-IPF: 18 mg BID slowed FVC decline by 68.8 mL vs placebo at week 52.
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: The newest FDA-approved IPF drug and the first with a new mechanism in over a decade. Cite FIBRONEER-IPF as ~69 mL less FVC lost at week 52 vs placebo (68.8 mL adjusted difference) — never invent 80 mL/year. List FIRST in Approved Treatments. Do NOT describe as investigational. Do NOT list as a repurposing candidate.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pirfenidone
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Pleiotropic anti-fibrotic; inhibits TGF-β-stimulated collagen synthesis and reduces fibroblast proliferation
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: FDA-approved first-line antifibrotic (with nintedanib and nerandomilast). Reduces ≥10% FVC decline or death by ~48% over 52 weeks (ASCEND). Do NOT list as a repurposing candidate — Section 3 only.

pipelineDrugs.name: Nintedanib
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Intracellular tyrosine kinase inhibitor — VEGFR, FGFR, PDGFR
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved 2014 for IPF (INPULSIS); 2019 for PPF (INBUILD); 2020 for SSc-ILD (SENSCIS)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: FDA-approved first-line antifibrotic. Reduces annual FVC decline by ~100-125 mL/year vs placebo. Also approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis and SSc-ILD. Do NOT list as a repurposing candidate — Section 3 only.

pipelineDrugs.name: BMS-986278
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Lysophosphatidic acid receptor 1 (LPA1) antagonist — blocks pro-fibrotic LPA signaling
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 3 (ALOFT-IPF / ALOFT-PPF) active, not recruiting; positive phase 2 readout 2023
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: LPA1 antagonism is a mechanistically distinct anti-fibrotic pathway. Phase 2 showed ~69% reduction in rate of FVC decline vs placebo at the 60 mg dose.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pamrevlumab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody targeting connective tissue growth factor (CTGF/CCN2)
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 3 ZEPHYRUS-1 failed primary endpoint (June 2023); development for IPF halted
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: High-profile failure in IPF. Patients who follow IPF news may still ask about it — needs to be addressed as discontinued for this indication.

pipelineDrugs.name: Inhaled treprostinil
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved for PH-ILD (INCREASE trial, 2021); investigational as antifibrotic (TETON-1, TETON-2 phase 3)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Unexpected signal in INCREASE suggested possible anti-fibrotic effect in addition to pulmonary hypertension benefit. TETON phase 3 trials tested this hypothesis head-on.

pipelineDrugs.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
pipelineDrugs.status: Failed in IPF (PANTHER-NAC 2014); under renewed investigation in TOLLIP-genotype-defined subgroup
pipelineDrugs.approvalStatus: not approved for IPF — OTC supplement
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Monotherapy NAC was negative in PANTHER-NAC. Ongoing pharmacogenomic work suggests the TOLLIP TT genotype subgroup may respond. Currently an open research question, not a treatment recommendation.

excludedAgents.name: Triple therapy (prednisone + azathioprine + N-acetylcysteine)
excludedAgents.reason: PANTHER-IPF (2012) was stopped early by DSMB for increased mortality (11% vs 1%) and hospitalization (29% vs 8%) vs placebo. STRONG guideline-level recommendation against.

excludedAgents.name: Prednisone monotherapy for stable IPF
excludedAgents.reason: No benefit shown in controlled studies. Chronic steroid harm (bone, glucose, infection). Different from acute exacerbation management where empirical steroids may be used despite weak evidence.

excludedAgents.name: N-acetylcysteine monotherapy (general IPF population)
excludedAgents.reason: PANTHER-NAC (2014) — no effect on FVC decline vs placebo in the overall IPF population. May be evaluated in TOLLIP TT-genotype subgroup (see pipelineDrugs).

excludedAgents.name: Offshore stem-cell therapy (clinics in China / Vietnam / Mexico / India)
excludedAgents.reason: No peer-reviewed efficacy data for IPF. Multiple FDA warning letters. Patient-safety concern, not scientific integrity of the literature.

excludedAgents.name: Metformin as an IPF antifibrotic
excludedAgents.reason: Metformin HAS been researched for IPF — it is NOT an unstudied drug. Lab studies in mice and in human IPF cells (Rangarajan, Nature Medicine 2018) showed metformin can reverse lung scarring, which created excitement. BUT the human data do not back this up: a post-hoc analysis of 624 patients across three phase 3 pirfenidone trials (Spagnolo, Respiration 2018) found metformin had no effect on lung-function decline, walking distance, hospitalization, or survival, and slightly more metformin users had a >=5% drop in FVC. A dedicated phase 3 trial is ongoing. Bottom line: studied in people, but not shown to help — not an established IPF treatment outside a trial. Never describe metformin as 'not researched' or 'never studied' for IPF.
